items.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022
items.q: as a matter of fact I have done a lot with Keith on a number of his singles and albums

ctx.x: I had a question about that, I’m glad you said that. If you did a review on a record and let’s say it was sort of in — well here we go with labels — but mainstream I guess, and you were struck by how swinging the rhythm section is, for you, what makes that work? What makes that rhythm section swing more than some other ones?

I think that swinging in that particular instance is something that derives an emotional and rhythmic response from me the listener. Okay? One can talk about before the beat, on the beat, behind the beat, you know all that technological stuff, but it’s all about emotion. So quite honestly it’ll be rare — at least in my experience — where the rhythm section is really swinging and the vocalist or the front line is let’s say a little bit less energetic. Okay? You know you have to look at a production in its…

you know what good balance is, and you know what good mixing is, and you appreciate the production elements and the production values of what goes into the artwork. You know it’s almost like, and there are samples of this, it’s almost like a beautiful classic painting that has a gaudy, gaudy frame. Okay? And it’s like well I’m interested in the Mona Lisa, I’m’ not interested in this you know, gilded peeing cherubs and whatever it happens to be. You know? So it really is an immersion. You know? You really immerse…
